task.title: Issue #39 RFC 9001 0-RTT policy
task.summary: The implementation plan is complete and the worker is editing the 0-RTT rejection, replay-protection, and application-policy paths.

causes.detail: The completed plan released the active worker attempt.

plan.objective: Make 0-RTT rejection a first-class connection transition, restore rejected writes for 1-RTT, reject acknowledgments of rejected packets, prevent server processing, and define safe replay policies.
plan.sourceContext: GitHub issue #39 / RFC 9001 Sections 4.6.2, 4.9.3, 5.6, and 9.2 / 13 Duvet requirements
constraints: Do not build a distributed replay database or cross-process anti-replay protocol.
Keep HTTP/3 application data and extensions handshake-gated.
Do not update the issue, commit, push, or modify generated reports.
validationCommands: focused 0-RTT connection, TLS, HTTP/0.9, and HTTP/3 tests

steps.title: Track terminal 0-RTT outcomes
steps.detail: Record every sent 0-RTT packet number, emit one terminal outcome, and discard the client write key on rejection.

steps.title: Enforce rejection semantics
steps.detail: Restore reliable stream data for 1-RTT, reject ACKs for rejected packets, and prevent server processing or acknowledgment.

steps.title: Define retry and key-discard policy
steps.detail: Preserve new packet numbers after Retry and use conservative server key discard when packet history has gaps.

steps.title: Restore TLS anti-replay
steps.detail: Use shared QuicTLS context state and reject unsafe BoringSSL server early-data acceptance.

steps.title: Define application profiles
steps.detail: Keep HTTP/3 handshake-gated and document HTTP/0.9 GET-only replay tolerance.

steps.title: Cover behavior and Duvet requirements
steps.detail: Add focused connection, recovery, TLS, and application tests for all 13 tracked requirements.

steps.title: Validate the patch
steps.detail: Run both TLS backend suites and the repository build and test gates.

transcript.label: Implementation strategy
transcript.text: Rejection needs exact packet bookkeeping so recovery accounting can be removed without declaring congestion loss while reliable STREAM data returns to the unsent path.
